general_rules.description: Internal team (same domain) receives casual tone with minimal greetings and no closing signature, regardless of seniority.
French external contacts (clients, investors, government) receive formal tone with 'Bonjour [Name],' greeting and 'Bien cordialement, Priya Pivot' closing.
English-speaking investors and external partners receive semi-formal tone with 'Hi [Name],' greeting and first-name-only closing.
Code-switching between French and English occurs with French colleagues when discussing product/technical topics; French dominates in opening but English used for technical details.
Emoji usage (🚀, 👌, 🔥, 🙏) appears in casual internal emails and semi-formal investor emails, but never in formal French business correspondence.
Action items and requests to internal team use imperative form without 'please' ('can you', 'tu peux', 'ship without slack').
Investor and client emails include structured lists, metrics, and specific dates; internal emails use bullet points or inline requests.
French formal emails include full legal signature (name + title) when corresponding with external parties; internal French emails omit signature.
Ultra-short responses to internal team ('just go 🚀', 'exactement ce que je pensais') signal approval without elaboration.
Enterprise deal discussions with internal team mix casual tone with detailed technical requirements (SAML, SCIM, data residency, SOC2).
